# Change the teleport power-up (P7) activation key

## Problem Statement
The teleport power-up (P7) is currently activated with the Space key. It needs to be changed to the S key or the down arrow key per product requirement.

## Users
- Player controlling the ship in the GymPowerUpsCombat scene — needs to activate teleport with S or down arrow instead of Space.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — New activation key:** The teleport power-up activates when the S key or down arrow is pressed (depending on clarification).
- **AC2 — Space key freed:** The Space key is no longer used for teleport activation (and continues to work for other purposes if applicable).
- **AC3 — GDD updated:** The Game Design Document (§3 Controls table, §4.4 P7 Teleport, §6.4) is updated to reflect the new key binding.
- **AC4 — Tests pass:** All existing tests pass; any tests that check for Space key triggering are updated.
- **AC5 — Full test suite passes.**

## Constraints
- Scope is the GymPowerUpsCombat.ts gym scene (main game scene scope TBD).
- Must maintain backward compatibility with test harness (triggerTeleport method).
- Must preserve the FIFO stack behavior and Phase Shift on arrival.

## Existing State
- Teleport activates on Space key (`spaceKey` in `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` line 272).
- GDD documents Space as the activation key across multiple sections.

## Desired Change
- Change teleport activation from Space to S or down arrow key.
- Update GDD to reflect new key binding.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Change `spaceKey` to use S or down arrow
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §3, §4.4, §6.4
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — Update any Space-key dependent tests

## Related Work
- AH-0MTE8EBZ1002U3PX — Unit tests: P7 Teleport (completed)
- AH-0MTE8EBAH007GUO0 — Effects module: teleport (completed)
- AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66 — Combat gym scene with teleport (completed)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** The S key is also used for movement (WASD). This could conflict with downward movement. *Mitigation: Clarify whether both S and down arrow should work, or just one.*
- **Assumption:** Only the gym scene needs updating; the main game scene does not yet have teleport activated.
- **Assumption:** Space key is not needed for shooting or other actions in the gym scene.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should teleport activate on EITHER the S key OR the down arrow key (both work)?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Should it be the S key with down arrow as an alternative?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Should the Space key still work for other actions (e.g., shooting)?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Is the scope limited to the gym scene (GymPowerUpsCombat.ts), or should the main game scene also be updated?" — Answer: **OPEN**
data.title: Change the activation key for teleport to s or the down arrow

# Make weapons cumulative and time out

## Headline

Replace the persistent weapon system with a cumulative, time-limited model: collecting a weapon power-up adds its firing effects to the ship's arsenal for 10 seconds, while the initial cannon remains permanent.

## Problem statement

The current weapon system uses a single-slot persistent model — collecting a weapon power-up **replaces** the currently equipped weapon with no timer. The operator has requested that weapons be **cumulative** (stacking effects) and **time out** after 10 seconds, with the exception of the initial cannon.

## Users

- **Player testing the game** — wants to collect multiple weapon power-ups and see their firing effects stack, then watch them expire one-by-one over 10 seconds, creating a dynamic and escalating combat experience.
- **Developer implementing the change** — needs a clear model for tracking multiple active weapons with individual timers and updating the Player entity, GymWeapons scene, and weapon utilities to support this behavior.

## Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to collect Spread while already firing the cannon so my ship fires *both* patterns, giving me more coverage without replacing my existing weapon.
- As a **player**, I want to see weapons I've collected time out after 10 seconds so that combat feels dynamic and power-ups create temporary bursts of capability rather than permanent upgrades.
- As a **player**, I want the initial cannon to **never time out** so I always have at least one reliable weapon.
- As a **player**, I want the Reset power-up to clear all timed weapons and leave only the cannon, giving me a way to "refresh" if I've lost all my timed weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cumulative weapons:** The Player entity tracks a **collection** of active weapons instead of a single equipped weapon. Collecting a weapon power-up adds it to the active set (no replacement). The cannon is always present in the active set.
- [ ] **AC2 — 10-second timeout per weapon:** Each weapon power-up (spread, dual, rapid) gets its own independent 10-second countdown from the moment of collection. When a timed weapon expires, it is removed from the active set and stops firing. The cannon has no timer and never expires.
- [ ] **AC3 — Auto-fire all active weapons:** On each fire cycle, the ship fires from **every active weapon** in the collection simultaneously. Each weapon fires at its own fire rate independently (e.g., rapid fires every 125ms, cannon every 400ms, spread every 600ms).
- [ ] **AC4 — Reset power-up clears timed weapons:** Collecting the Reset power-up removes all timed weapons (spread, dual, rapid) from the active set, leaving only the permanent cannon. The Reset power-up itself is not a weapon and is never added to the active set.
- [ ] **AC5 — GymWeapons scene updated:** The GymWeapons scene correctly handles the new cumulative model — collecting drops adds weapons to the active set, the Reset drop clears timed weapons, expired weapons are silently dropped, and auto-fire fires from all active weapons.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing:** Unit tests verify: weapon collection adds to active set, individual weapon timers count down and expire, expired weapons are removed, cannon never expires, Reset clears all timed weapons, auto-fire emits bullets from all active weapons at correct rates. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the cumulative + timed weapon semantics (GDD §4.4 revision, code comments, README).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic.
- **Threat-free gym:** no enemies, no enemy bullets, no collision damage — player bullets are demonstration-only.
- **Backward compatibility:** the GymWeapons scene must continue to work with the new model.
- **Existing code to refactor:** Player.ts (single `_equippedWeapon` → weapon collection with timers), weapons.ts (add timeout tracking helpers if needed), GymWeapons.ts (collection logic update).

## Existing state

- `Player.ts` (`src/entities/Player.ts`): single `_equippedWeapon: WeaponId` slot, `equipWeapon()`, `resetWeapon()`, `tryFire()` fires one weapon.
- `weapons.ts` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`): weapon catalogue with definitions for cannon, spread, dual, rapid — all persistent, no timeout model.
- `GymWeapons.ts` (`src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`): `_collectDrop()` calls `player.equipWeapon()` or `player.resetWeapon()` — single-slot model.
- Weapon power-up drops: Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset — round-robin, 7-second lifetime on screen.

## Desired change

1. **Player entity — weapon collection:** Replace `_equippedWeapon: WeaponId` with a weapon collection (e.g., a `Set<WeaponId>` for permanent weapons and a `Map<WeaponId, number>` for timed weapons tracking expiry timestamps). Update `equipWeapon()` to **add** to the collection, `resetWeapon()` to clear timed weapons.
2. **Player entity — auto-fire all weapons:** Update `tryFire()` to fire from **every active weapon** in the collection. Each weapon maintains its own cooldown. Emit bullets for all weapons whose cooldowns have elapsed this frame.
3. **Weapon timeout tracking:** Add per-weapon countdown logic. When a timed weapon's 10-second timer expires, remove it from the active set. Expose a method to tick and cull expired weapons.
4. **GymWeapons scene — updated collection:** Update `_collectDrop()` to call the new cumulative `equipWeapon()` (add, not replace). Reset clears timed weapons. No changes to the drop spawner itself.
5. **Constants:** Add a tunable `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000` constant (10 seconds) to `core/constants.ts`.
6. **Tests and documentation.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — major refactor: weapon collection with timers, multi-weapon auto-fire
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — add timeout tracking helpers, possibly a `WeaponInstance` type with expiry
- `src/core/constants.ts` — add `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — update collection logic for cumulative model
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — new tests for cumulative weapon behavior
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — update tests for cumulative model

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — breaking GymWeapons tests:** The existing scene tests assert single-weapon behavior. They will need updates. Mitigated: tests are well-structured and the changes are contained to Player + GymWeapons.
- **Risk — auto-fire complexity with multiple weapons:** Each weapon has its own cooldown; the firing logic must track cooldowns per-weapon. Mitigated: straightforward extension of the existing cooldown pattern.
- **Risk — visual clutter from multi-weapon bullets:** With 3-4 weapons firing simultaneously, the screen may be visually busy. Mitigated: bullets have distinct colors per weapon (existing palette supports this).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD display for active weapons and remaining timers is **out of scope** — this is a gameplay mechanic change, not a UI change.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (completed): the item that implemented the current persistent single-slot weapon system. This item **refactors** that system.
- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (completed): generic power-up infrastructure.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Weapon stacking model — when collecting Spread while having cannon, does the ship fire BOTH patterns simultaneously (cannon + spread), and if then collecting Dual, does it fire ALL three (cannon + spread + dual)?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.
- Q2: "Timeout granularity — does each weapon power-up get its own independent 10-second timer (e.g., Spread collected at t=0 expires at t=10, Dual collected at t=5 expires at t=15), or does picking up any weapon reset ALL active weapon timers to 10 seconds?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.
- Q3: "Reset power-up behavior — with cumulative weapons, does Reset clear ALL timed weapons leaving only cannon, or does it work differently?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.
- Q4: "Any visual/audio feedback on weapon expiration? Or do timed weapons simply stop firing when their timer expires?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.

> All questions marked OPEN — waiting for producer review.

# Player should spawn center screen

## Problem statement

In the enemy gym scenes, the player ship spawns at the top-right corner of the screen `(920, 30)` — behind the HUD area — instead of at center screen.

## Users

- **Players** — when entering an enemy gym scene, the player ship should be clearly visible and centered on screen, not tucked into a corner behind UI elements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Center spawn:** The player ship spawns at the center of the game screen in all enemy gym scenes (GymEnemies, GymBoss, GymPowerUps, GymPowerUpsCombat, GymWeapons).
2. **AC2 — Consistent across all gym scenes:** The spawn position is uniform across every gym scene that includes a player ship.
3. **AC3 — Visible and unobstructed:** The spawn position places the player ship clear of any HUD elements and enemy formations.
4. **AC4 — Respawn consistency:** When the player is hit and respawns (in scenes that support hits), the respawn position matches the initial spawn position (center screen).
5. **AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The change is a single constant update in `src/core/constants.ts` (`PLAYER_SPAWN`).
- The existing `GymBoss` scene already uses its own spawn coordinates (`BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_X`, `BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_Y` at center-bottom) and should remain unaffected unless specified otherwise.
- The `GymPlayer` scene already spawns at center screen and should be unaffected.

## Existing state

- `PLAYER_SPAWN` in `src/core/constants.ts` is set to `{ x: 920, y: 30 }` (top-right corner).
- The constant's comment explains the rationale: "clear of every formation and firing rightward off-screen so boot-time auto-fire never interferes with formation or wait-based tests."
- Used by: `GymEnemies.ts` (player toggle, config), `GymFormationScene` (base class), and related test files.
- `GymBoss` uses separate constants `BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_X` / `BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_Y` (center-bottom).

## Desired change

Update `PLAYER_SPAWN` to `{ x: GAME_WIDTH / 2, y: GAME_HEIGHT / 2 }` — i.e., `{ x: 480, y: 270 }` — so the player spawns at the center of the screen in enemy gym scenes.

Update the constant's comment to reflect the new intent.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Change `PLAYER_SPAWN` value and update its comment.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Uses `PLAYER_SPAWN`; tests may need updating.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Base class; player position derived from config.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Tests reference `PLAYER_SPAWN` coordinates; may need updates.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — Tests assert player position against `PLAYER_SPAWN`; may need updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** — Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (consolidated gym scene base class).
- **AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66** — Combat gym scene: GymPowerUpsCombat.
- **AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9** — Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Auto-fire on scene boot now fires from center screen instead of the edge. This could interfere with enemy formations earlier. **Mitigation:** The formation starts off-screen and drifts rightward; the player's bullets travel in the direction of travel (velocity heading), so this should be fine.
- **Assumption:** "Behind the hud bar" refers to visual obstruction at the top-right; center screen resolves this for all HUD configurations.
- **Assumption:** `GymBoss` should keep its existing center-bottom spawn position (its own constants are separate).
- **Risk:** Tests that assert specific player coordinates at scene start will need updating.

## Effort & Risk

- **Effort:** Small — single constant change + comment update + test adjustments.
- **Risk:** Low — the change is localized to spawn position; no new logic introduced.
